messages.subject: knitr & Lyx: Windows metafile conversion
parts:
Hello knitrs,

I'm having problems with Windows metafiles - unfortunately I have to
use them.

Lyx does a good job of converting them when added manually through
menus, using conversion tool http://wiki.lyx.org/Windows/MetafileToEPSConverter
. I get the impression that this converts the metafile to a .png,
which is then converted to eps. The output looks excellent.

However, when using knitr with' dev = win.metafile' in chunk options,
this isn't activated, and when compiling, an error message appears
that a file (with the chunk name) can't be found with an acceptable
extension. I'm assuming that this is because the file hasn't been
converted.

I've been writing a few hooks for various things recently, but am
unsure about how to go about this one, as I'm brand spanking new to
LaTex, knir, and Lyx.

I've exported my Lyx file to .tex ("LaTex (pdflatex)"), and have a
look through the code.

For manually inserted (and thus converted) files, the includegraphics
macro points to an eps file, the name of which is the entire file
path with underscores instead of slashes, (and is not in the \figure
folder), and in the output produced by the knitr chunk, the
includegraphics macro points to a file in the \figure folder, of the
name of the chunk, with no extension specified.

In other words I can't see where the conversion process happens, or
how to force it from within knitr.

Does anyone have any ideas about how I might be able to write the
conversion process into a hook?

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr & Lyx: Windows metafile conversion
parts:
Hi,

Briefly speaking, this is just a system() call to metafile2eps.exe
using a chunk hook, and it is very similar to the hook_pdfcrop()
function: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/R/hooks.R

Read more about chunk hooks and see if you can DIY:
http://yihui.name/knitr/hooks I can help if you cannot figure it out.

Note knitr does not write the filename extension to the tex output,
e.g. for foo.eps, it only write \includegraphics{foo} instead of
\includegraphics{foo.eps}, therefore all you need to do is to convert
the metafile to eps, and you do not need to worry about the tex file
since it does not need to be changed. LaTeX complained because it
could note find an plot file with an expected extension (wmf is not
supported).

Also note eps does not work with pdflatex, if I remember correctly (I
have not used postscript for a few years, so I may be wrong). You may
still go to pdf finally. So I'm curious what is the particular reason
that you have to use windows metafile?

------

The other lazy approach is to use chunk option include=FALSE to
suppress the output completely, but the plot file will be generated as
usual; then you can insert the file into LyX, and let LyX convert it
for you. In this approach your document is no longer completely
dynamic.

Regards,
Yihui
